kw.name: Open Bench
kw.msg: Set suite metadata 'Radio' to value 'Connect Systems CS7000-PLUS (cs7000p)'.
Set suite metadata 'Calibration' to value 'assumed, measured 2026-10-20 (d55ce4aa0a3c)'.
Set suite metadata 'Suite commit' to value '1d00f71740'.
kw.doc: Load the bench, its calibration and the radio file, and prepare the instruments. All five are mandatory and differ from tester to tester, so suites take them from the command line (-v BENCH:... and so on). `firmware` names what the radio runs, such as a git describe; `hardware` names the unit, by model and serial number, since units of one model measure differently. `dsp` names the DSP image the radio's audio processor runs, such as its sha256; it is mandatory for radio files with dsp_image: true, whose firmware states can differ in it alone.

kw.name: Run Tag
kw.doc: Four hex digits that differ from run to run, to put in test traffic: the radio's de-duplication then can't mistake a rerun's packets for the last run's, nor can the operator.

kw.name: Set Suite Variable
kw.doc: Makes the variable available everywhere within the scope of the current suite.

test.name: 70cm: APRS RX Stores A Message For My Callsign

kw.name: Use Band
kw.doc: Make a band from the radio file current: captures and transmissions use its frequency. Sets ${BAND} and ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} for the test. oat.expand calls it in each per-band test's setup.

kw.name: Operator Does
kw.arg: Set the radio to APRS on ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} MHz (25 kHz FM), with Settings > APRS > Callsign ${APRS_CALLSIGN}, and open the inbox. This run's messages end their tag in ".${RUN}"
kw.doc: Ask the operator to do something and wait until it's done.

kw.name: Aprs Message
kw.doc: An APRS message's information field, :ADDRESSEE:text{number, for Start Transmitting APRS Packets.

kw.name: Send APRS Packets
Start Transmitting Aprs Packets
kw.doc: Send APRS packets on the test frequency: TXDELAY of flags, the AX.25 UI frames from `source` via `path` (digipeaters separated by commas, a * marking one that has repeated it, empty for none), then gap_s without carrier. Each transmission carries per_transmission frames back to back, one flag apart, as a TNC empties its queue. deviation_hz is the louder tone's peak deviation; twist_db raises the space tone over the mark, as a pre-emphasizing transmitter does (aprs.PREEMPHASIS_TWIST_DB, 5.3 dB), or lowers it when negative. offset_hz moves the carrier off frequency and baud_error_ppm the bit rate off 1200. The level is level_dbm at the radio, level_db relative to the bench's gain, or the bench's gain. Plays once unless loop; returns how long one pass lasts, in seconds, to wait before Stop Transmitting.

kw.name: Wait Seconds
kw.doc: Let time pass on the bench (at once on the simulated one).

kw.name: Stop Transmitting
kw.doc: Stop the transmitter.
Send packets with Start Transmitting APRS Packets, wait until they're out, then stop the transmitter.

kw.name: Operator Confirms
kw.arg: The inbox shows one new APRS message from ${SENDER}: "oat1.${RUN} hello from the bench"
kw.doc: Ask the operator a yes/no question; fail the test on no.

test.doc: APRS-RX-1: a message to the radio's APRS callsign arrives in the inbox, from the sender, with its text.

kw.doc: Stop the instruments and write measurements.json: every capture, check and operator answer, with the run's provenance. Absolute paths are made relative, so the file can be published as it is.

suite.doc:
APRS on receive (OpenRTX#559): the transmitter sends APRS packets (oat.aprs: AX.25 UI frames as 1200 baud Bell 202 AFSK on FM, checked against Dire Wolf) and messages addressed to the radio's APRS callsign must land in its inbox, once each, and nothing else.
Until the radio can report its inbox over a data link, the operator reads it: every message carries a short tag ("oat1.7f2a", "oat2.7f2a"...) to look for, whose second half differs from run to run (Run Tag). A rerun's messages are new messages, then: the radio mustn't treat them as copies of the last run's, nor the operator mistake the last run's for them. No audio interface is needed. The radio file decides where APRS runs (mode:aprs on a band).

suite.name: Performance

kw.name: Open Bench
kw.msg: Set suite metadata 'Radio' to value 'Connect Systems CS7000-PLUS (cs7000p)'.
Set suite metadata 'Calibration' to value 'assumed, measured 2026-10-20 (d55ce4aa0a3c)'.
Set suite metadata 'Suite commit' to value '1d00f71740'.
kw.doc: Load the bench, its calibration and the radio file, and prepare the instruments. All five are mandatory and differ from tester to tester, so suites take them from the command line (-v BENCH:... and so on). `firmware` names what the radio runs, such as a git describe; `hardware` names the unit, by model and serial number, since units of one model measure differently. `dsp` names the DSP image the radio's audio processor runs, such as its sha256; it is mandatory for radio files with dsp_image: true, whose firmware states can differ in it alone.

test.name: 70cm: APRS Perf Every Frame Heard At The Bench Level

kw.name: Use Band
kw.doc: Make a band from the radio file current: captures and transmissions use its frequency. Sets ${BAND} and ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} for the test. oat.expand calls it in each per-band test's setup.

kw.name: Set Up APRS TNC
Operator Does
kw.arg: Set the radio to APRS on ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} MHz (25 kHz FM), with its USB port connected to the bench's TNC port and nothing else reading it
kw.doc: Ask the operator to do something and wait until it's done.

kw.name: Set To Dictionary
kw.doc: Adds the given `key_value_pairs` and/or `items` to the `dictionary`.
Once per band: the radio in APRS mode on the band's frequency and its TNC port connected.

kw.name: Send Aprs Test Frames
kw.doc: Send `count` numbered test frames and count what the radio's TNC reported. kind is status (short status reports), full (eight digipeaters and a 256-byte information field: the largest frame), or escapes (a full-size frame full of the bytes KISS must escape, 0xC0 and 0xDB). Every frame carries the run tag and its number, so each is accounted for: heard, missing, heard more than once, or corrupt (ours, but different from what was sent). Takes Start Transmitting APRS Packets' options. Returns the counts and the fraction heard.

kw.name: Aprs Frames Should Be Heard
kw.doc: Fail unless the radio reported at least `minimum` of the frames (the radio file's aprs.min_frame_rate when not given), and none corrupt or twice.

test.doc: APRS-PERF-1: at the bench's level, nominal deviation and no twist, the radio reports every frame (aprs.min_frame_rate), exactly as sent, once.

kw.name: Find Aprs Sensitivity
kw.msg: Set test message to: 90% at -6.0, 50% at -8.5 dB re bench
kw.doc: Step the level down from `start` to `stop`, sending `count` test frames at each, until fewer than half are heard; the result has the curve and the levels where 90% and 50% of frames were still heard, interpolated. Levels are dBm at the radio with a transmitter level table (or absolute: true), otherwise dB relative to the bench's gain; compare relative results only within one session, on one bench. Takes Send APRS Test Frames' options.

test.doc: APRS-PERF-3: the frame rate as the level falls, and the levels where 90% and 50% of frames are still heard. Recorded for comparison; no limit yet.

kw.doc: Send `count` numbered test frames and count what the radio's TNC reported. kind is status (short status reports), full (eight digipeaters and a 256-byte information field: the largest frame), or escapes (a full-size frame full of the bytes KISS must escape, 0xC0 and 0xDB). Every frame carries the run tag and its number, so each is accounted for: heard, missing, heard more than once, or corrupt (ours, but different from what was sent). Takes Start Transmitting APRS Packets' options. Returns the counts and the fraction heard.

kw.name: Close Bench
kw.doc: Stop the instruments and write measurements.json: every capture, check and operator answer, with the run's provenance. Absolute paths are made relative, so the file can be published as it is.

suite.doc:
APRS receive performance, read from the radio's KISS TNC: the transmitter sends numbered test frames and the radio reports every frame it decodes on its serial port (the bench's tnc section), so each one is accounted for without an operator. Frames carry the run tag, so reruns and other traffic don't count.
The radio's ordinary APRS receive is what's measured: the TNC only copies out what the demodulator and frame decoder hand to the inbox. Levels are relative to the bench's gain unless ABSOLUTE_LEVELS is true and the calibration has a transmitter level table; relative results compare firmware only within one session on one bench. Limits are the radio file's aprs section. Tag "long" marks the soak.
